newsitem.title: CANADA: WIC appeal ruling due Thursday-lawyers.
newsitem.headline: WIC appeal ruling due Thursday-lawyers.

text.p: The British Columbia Court of Appeal will announce its ruling in a case involving Canadian broadcaster WIC Western International Communications Ltd on Thursday, lawyers involved in the case said.
The case is an appeal of a decision last year that effectively blocked CanWest Global Communications Corp's C$636 million takeover bid for WIC.

The case, brought by two former WIC directors and supported by CanWest, sought to have voting rights awarded to WIC's non-voting shareholders. The British Columbia Supreme Court ruled against them last year and the case was appealed to the Court of Appeal.
If the appeal succeeds, WIC would be vulnerable to a takeover bid, analysts have said.

WIC owns some of the most valuable properties in Canadian broadcasting including eight television, 12 radio stations and a share of Canada's CTV network. It has faced mounting shareholder unrest amid complaints the company has performed poorly and is unresponsive to stockholders.

The Griffiths family of Vancouver, which founded the company, controls WIC because it owns most of the voting Class A shares even though it holds only seven percent of WIC's total equity. The two-tier share structure has been a major target of shareholder complaint.
CanWest recently announced it purchased another block of WIC non-voting B shares, bringing its holding to 15 percent. It said it believes itself to be the company's biggest holder of the B shares.
The court registry said the decision would be delivered at 1700 EST.
